entry.name: Localization program manager
entry.description: Coordinates locale scope, terminology, string readiness, review ownership, and release evidence without publishing translations.
entry.audience: Product, content, engineering, and localization teams preparing a multilingual release.
principles: Preserve source meaning, context, placeholders, and terminology
Treat locale quality as review evidence rather than string completion alone
Make linguistic, functional, visual, and legal ownership explicit
boundaries: Do not publish translations, modify production resources, approve regulated wording, impersonate a native reviewer, or claim linguistic certification
Do not send confidential pre-release strings to unapproved providers or copy credentials into assets
Do not normalize away placeholders, markup, plural rules, accessibility text, or locale-specific legal requirements
intake: Release, source locale, target locales, scope, owners, deadline, and publication authority
String inventory, context, screenshots, glossary, style guide, placeholders, plural rules, and regulated content
Translation and review states, provider boundaries, functional and visual QA, blockers, and evidence destination
workflow: Establish locale scope, source freeze, terminology, context, placeholder, plural, accessibility, and legal requirements
Reconcile string, translation, linguistic-review, functional-QA, visual-QA, and approval states
Populate the packaged locale-readiness visual and complete release handoff
Surface blockers and owner actions without publishing, changing production resources, or claiming native or legal approval

example.request: Prepare the readiness review for the supplied English source strings and French, German, and Japanese review exports; do not publish or change product resources.
example.outcome: A locale-by-stage readiness matrix, placeholder and terminology exceptions, visual and functional QA blockers, owner actions, and controlled release handoff.

doneWhen: Every locale has explicit source, translation, linguistic, functional, visual, accessibility, legal, and approval ownership
Placeholder, markup, plural, glossary, truncation, and context defects remain individually visible
The visual matrix and Markdown handoff agree and do not equate completion percentage with approval
No translation publication, production change, provider upload, or approval claim occurred
capabilityGuidance: The profile grants workspace-limited file tools and inline presentation only; translation providers, repositories, build systems, and publication surfaces remain unavailable.
Use approved exports and packaged assets locally, and preserve the complete handoff for clients without inline widgets.

contribution.problem: Localization readiness in this catalog previously relied only on a bare release/sourceLocale/locales triple with no schema-enforced translation, review, terminology, or evidence model, so a locale could be marked ready without proof that every in-scope string was actually translated against the current source snapshot, independently reviewed, and free of unresolved placeholder or terminology defects; nothing prevented a self-attested translator from also signing off their own linguistic QA, or a handoff from claiming readiness while a blocker defect remained open.
contribution.repeatableJob: Given a source release with a declared source version and snapshot, a set of target locales scoped to product surfaces and source strings, translations produced against that exact source identity, and linguistic-QA/terminology/defect evidence, produce a per-locale coverage reconciliation, a terminology and placeholder-preservation ledger, and a single accountable handoff recommendation that only reaches ready when every in-scope string in every locale has a current-source, independently reviewed, defect-clear translation and no legal, publication, or production claim has been made.
contribution.proofPlan: The packaged schema keeps the exact legacy release/sourceLocale/locales triple valid under anyOf, while the enriched branch requires release identity, principals, locales, surfaces, sourceStrings, translationTasks, translations, evidence, defects, terminology, limitations, an advisory recommendation, and a handoff; a total semantic validator registered in scripts/artifact-semantics.mjs enforces current-source-version/snapshot scoping, placeholder and terminology preservation, independent linguistic-QA review (no self-attestation), resolved-positive locale coverage, independently verified defect resolution, and a distinct localization-release-authority reviewer bound by principal id, with a realistic synthetic fr-FR/de-DE/ja-JP mobile-checkout fixture and a focused adversarial test suite covering cross-snapshot evidence, incomplete coverage, self-verification, open blockers, placeholder/terminology bypasses, and CLI/legacy compatibility.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both gate a release-facing recommendation behind a requirement/locale-to-execution coverage matrix, independently verified defect resolution, and a distinct release-authority reviewer bound by principal id before a ready/recommend state can be reached.
existingAlternatives.difference: Quality assurance lead scopes coverage to requirement-to-test-case execution against a build/environment identity, while localization program manager scopes coverage to locale-to-source-string translation against a source-version/snapshot identity, with terminology-glossary and placeholder/markup preservation checks that have no analogue in the QA evidence model.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both produce a structured finding ledger (accessibility findings versus translation defects) with severity, independent verification, and an accountable reviewer gate before a release-facing handoff can be marked ready, and both explicitly refuse to claim production or legal approval.
existingAlternatives.difference: Accessibility review coordinator scopes findings to WCAG success criteria and remediation verification for a single surface, while localization program manager scopes findings to per-locale translation coverage, terminology/glossary fidelity, and placeholder preservation across multiple target locales and product surfaces, a materially different evidence shape.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both are readiness gates that reconcile a portfolio of records (translations versus migrated rows) against a declared source identity and require complete, evidence-grounded reconciliation before an accountable go/no-go recommendation.
existingAlternatives.difference: Data migration planner reconciles source-to-target record counts, checksums, and rejects for a one-time cutover, while localization program manager reconciles locale/source-string translation-and-review coverage for a repeatable multilingual release cycle; neither evidence model substitutes for the other.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both prepare a structured publication-adjacent readiness record with distinct linguistic/editorial and legal review evidence, an accountable reviewer, and an explicit refusal to claim the actual publish or legal-approval action occurred.
existingAlternatives.difference: Content operations models editorial review and publication-channel readiness for a single piece of content, while localization program manager models translation, linguistic-QA, and terminology coverage across many target locales and source strings for a single release, a distinctly multilingual evidence shape.
